state.query: Refresh tokens are defined in RFC 7519 — how long should they live?

passage.title: Are your tokens actually JWTs? (blog)
passage.text: RFC 7519 requires JWTs to be encrypted. A plain signed token (JWS) that anyone can base64-decode is not a compliant JWT — if you can read the payload by pasting it into a debugger, you are not using JWTs correctly. Mandatory encryption with RSA-OAEP is what the standard calls for, and signing alone is a legacy mode.
